title: I really love Taiwan
goal: Give opinions and reasons in long sentences — and wrap up the whole course with one conversation that uses almost everything you've learned.
bekal: give opinions with 覺得 and reasons with 因為…所以…
build long sentences with 雖然…但是… and 不但…而且…
close a conversation warmly, the Taiwanese way

dialogs.title: 對話 — 最後一堂課
dialogs.intro: The semester is over. The three of them sit in the same milk tea shop as on the very first day.

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.id: Budi, a semester goes by so fast!
lines.literal: Budi, one — (measure word) — study-term — pass — (manner) — so — fast — (softener)!

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.id: It really does! It feels like I only arrived yesterday.
lines.literal: real — (one)! I — feel — seem — yesterday — only-just — arrive.

lines.speaker: 阿明:
lines.id: Your Chinese has improved so much!

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [因為|Yīnwèi][你們|nǐmen][很|hěn][有|yǒu][耐心|nàixīn]，[所以|suǒyǐ][我|wǒ][敢|gǎn][說|shuō]。
lines.id: Because you were all so patient, I dared to speak.
lines.literal: because — you (plural) — very — have — patience, so — I — dare — speak.

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.id: What do you like most about Taiwan?

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [人|Rén]。[雖然|Suīrán][我|wǒ][是|shì][外國人|wàiguó rén]，[但是|dànshì][大家|dàjiā][都|dōu][很|hěn][照顧|zhàogù][我|wǒ]。
lines.id: The people. Even though I'm a foreigner, everyone looked after me.
lines.literal: person. although — I — am — foreigner, but — everyone — all — very — take-care-of — me.

lines.speaker: 阿明:
lines.text: [台灣|Táiwān][最|zuì][美|měi][的|de][風景|fēngjǐng][是|shì][人|rén]。[我們|Wǒmen][常|cháng][這樣|zhèyàng][說|shuō]。
lines.id: The most beautiful scenery in Taiwan is its people. We say that a lot.
lines.literal: Taiwan — most — beautiful — 的 — scenery — is — person. we — often — this-way — say.

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [還有|Hái yǒu][食物|shíwù]！[不但|Búdàn][便宜|piányí]，[而且|érqiě][好吃|hǎochī]。
lines.id: And the food! Not only cheap, but tasty too.
lines.literal: also — have — food! not-only — cheap, moreover — tasty.

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.id: Will you come back next semester?
lines.literal: you — next — semester — still — will — come-back — (question)?

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [我|Wǒ][正在|zhèngzài][申請|shēnqǐng][獎學金|jiǎngxuéjīn]。[如果|Rúguǒ][申請|shēnqǐng][得到|dédào]，[我|wǒ][就|jiù][回來|huílái]。
lines.id: I'm applying for a scholarship. If I get it, I'll come back.
lines.literal: I — (in progress) — apply — reward-study-money. if — apply — get, I — then — come-back.

lines.speaker: 阿明:
lines.text: [一定|Yídìng][可以|kěyǐ][的|de]！[我|Wǒ][幫|bāng][你|nǐ][去|qù][廟|miào][拜拜|bàibài]！
lines.id: You'll definitely get it! I'll go pray for you at the temple!
lines.literal: surely — can — (one)! I — help — you — go — temple — worship!

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.id: Haha, thank you! I'll really miss you all.
lines.literal: haha, thanks! I — will — very — miss — you (plural).

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.id: Taiwan will always be your second home.
lines.literal: Taiwan — forever — is — you — 's — second — (measure word) — home.

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [那|Nà][我|wǒ][說|shuō][「再見」|zàijiàn]，[不|bù][說|shuō][「掰掰」|bāibāi]。[因為|Yīnwèi][我|wǒ][會|huì][再|zài][見|jiàn][你們|nǐmen]。
lines.id: Then I'll say "zaijian", not "baibai". Because I will see you again.
lines.literal: then — I — say — again-see, not — say — bye-bye. because — I — will — again — see — you (plural).

notes: ⚠️ **Budi's last line is a play on words that Taiwanese people really use.** 再見 literally means "see again", so choosing it over 掰掰 ("bye-bye") is a subtle way of saying "this isn't goodbye". You now know enough Mandarin to get wordplay like this.
**「台灣最美的風景是人」 is a genuinely famous line in Taiwan** — it came from a 2012 magazine article and has been repeated everywhere since, sometimes proudly, sometimes cynically.
**The 得 in 過得好快 is the manner marker** from unit 16: verb + 得 + adjective. 過得很快 (goes by fast), 睡得很好 (sleeps well), 學得很快 (learns fast).

**才 means "only just" or "not until"** and stresses that something happened later or less than expected: *昨天才到* (only arrived yesterday), *他八點才來* (he didn't come until eight). ⚠️ Its opposite is 就, which stresses earlier: *他六點就來了*.

**獎學金 (scholarship) is a very useful word** if you plan to study in Taiwan. The Huayu Enrichment Scholarship (HES) from Taiwan's Ministry of Education and the MOFA scholarship are two of the most popular with international students.

grammars.title: 覺得, 認為, 希望: giving opinions
body: **覺得** is the most common opinion verb. It's followed by **a whole clause**, not a noun — and Mandarin uses no linking word like "that".
after: ⚠️ **There's no word for "that".** *我覺得台灣很好* — straight on, no linker. Adding something in the middle is a mistake carried over from English "I think that…".
**覺得 is softer than 認為.** 覺得 is a personal feeling ("I feel"); 認為 is a considered opinion ("I believe"), more formal and more firm. In everyday conversation, it's almost always 覺得.
**覺得 also means "feel" physically**: *我覺得不舒服* (I don't feel well), *我覺得很累* (I feel tired).

grammars.title: Paired connectors: two words, one long sentence
body: Mandarin likes to use a **pair** of connectors, one in each half of the sentence. English usually needs just one, so beginners often forget the partner.
after: ⚠️ **Both halves can be used together**, unlike English, which forbids "although… but…". *雖然很貴，但是很好吃* is the most natural form in Mandarin, and dropping one half actually feels incomplete.

**These seven pairs are your tools for leveling up.** As long as your sentences are short, you still sound like a beginner; once you use paired connectors, you instantly sound like someone who really speaks Mandarin. Use one in every conversation starting today.

blocks.text: ⚠️ **真的假的？ ("true or false?") is the most typically Taiwanese reaction of surprise.** It's not an accusation; it's just an excited "seriously?". You'll hear it every time you share something surprising, and using it yourself makes you sound local instantly.
Twenty units, and here's what you take home. Read this list slowly; much of it will surprise you, because you learned it without feeling like you were memorizing anything.

items: **Reading pīnyīn correctly**, including the six tricky letters and the four curled-tongue sounds — plus the basics of 注音, used all over Taiwan.
**The four tones and their three change rules** — back-to-back third tones, 不, and 一.
**Building complete sentences**: subject – adverbial – verb – object, with time and place always before the verb.
**Asking questions six ways**: 嗎, question word in the answer's slot, A-不-A, 呢, 好嗎, and the typically Taiwanese 有…嗎.
**Measure words** — the wall that trips up English speakers most often, now behind you.
**Time, dates, numbers into the tens of thousands, and money** in 塊, the way Taiwanese people say it.
**Three kinds of "can" (會/能/可以) and three kinds of "want" (要/想/打算)**, which English often squeezes into just two words.
**了, 過, 在, and 有 + verb** — the whole A1 aspect system, including the Taiwanese touches.
**Result and potential complements** — 聽得懂, 買不到, 來不及.
**Building long sentences** with 的 and seven paired connectors.

blocks.title: And more important than all of that
items: You can **order a drink with exactly the sugar and ice you like** — the unofficial membership test of Taiwanese society.
You know **when to say 不好意思 and when to say 對不起**.
You know **never to give a clock as a gift**, and you know why.
You can say **我聽不懂，請說慢一點** without embarrassment — and that's the sentence that decides most whether you'll keep moving forward.
⚠️ And you know that **很 doesn't mean "very"**. Ten out of ten beginners don't know this.

blocks.text: **加油 literally means "add oil"** — like refueling. It's used to cheer on anyone who's working hard at something: an exam, a job, a match, or learning Mandarin. It's the last word of this course, and the most fitting one: **加油！**

answers: 我覺得台灣很好玩。 — 因為下雨，所以我沒去。 — 雖然很貴，但是很好吃。 — 不但便宜，而且好吃。 — 如果你來，我就很開心。 — 我會想你們。
所以 — 雖然 — 而且 — 如果 — 再 — 就

I think Taiwanese street food is not only cheap but also tasty. — Although I'm a foreigner, everyone looks after me. — Because I really love Taiwan, I want to come back again. — If I get the scholarship, I'll come back. — The place I like most is Tainan.
